source_text: Res clara est et iam in primo opere sufficienter impleta; verum quoniam tu adeo pellax esse voluisti, ut aliquam inter te et Manichaeum distinctionem facere nitereris, ideo necesse mihi nunc est urgere causam, ut non solum praeteritis dictis tuis, sed etiam, si qua deinceps inferre tentaveris, clareat obviatum. Dicimus itaque tam bonum esse opus Dei in nascente, ut ea quae substantiae eius sunt naturalia opus emendatore non habeant, quoniam, quicumque censuerit, id quod a Deo factum confitetur, aliter fieri debuisse, illum sine dubio reprehendit, quem corrigendae in alteram formam creaturae confitetur artificem.
pass_a_gloss: The thing is clear and already in the first work sufficiently filled; but since you have wanted to be so deceitful that you would strive to make some distinction between you and the Manichaean, therefore it is necessary for me now to urge the cause, that it be clear it has been met not only by your past sayings but also if you have tried to bring any thereafter. We say therefore that the work of God in one being born is so good that those things which are natural of its substance do not have need of an emender, since whoever has judged that that which he confesses made by God ought to have been made otherwise, without doubt reprehends him whom he confesses the craftsman of a creature to be corrected into another form.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: The matter is clear and was sufficiently established in my first work. Yet because you wanted to be so deceitful as to attempt a distinction between yourself and Mani, I must now press the case. It must be clear that we have answered not only your past statements but also anything you may try to introduce afterward. We say, therefore, that God’s work in a newborn is so good that the natural characteristics of its substance need no corrector. Anyone who judges that what he acknowledges God made ought to have been made differently undoubtedly criticizes the one he acknowledges as the maker of a creature supposedly needing correction into another form.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
